introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2021. Duration: TWO AND A HALF (2 1/2) HOURS.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Questions ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées sans source consultable. Aucune statistique précise n'est avancée sauf mention contraire ; les exemples cités sont des exemples reconnus. Les faits cités sont à faire relire par un géographe avant toute mise en avant.

Fond de carte 6(a) : le candidat doit placer les éléments sur la feuille fournie ; le corrigé décrit les positions (nord en haut, sans parallèles ni méridiens sur le fond de carte) et ne présente pas de carte annotée : les positions sont approximatives. Tracé du pipeline Tchad-Cameroun cité de façon générale (entrée par l'est, terminal à Kribi).

Faits à faire vérifier : pluviométrie « environ 1 500 à 2 000 mm ou plus » et température moyenne « environ 25 °C » de la région équatoriale (ordres de grandeur, aucune station citée) ; zone de forêt équatoriale limitée au nord vers 5 à 6 degrés de latitude nord.

questions.enonce_markdown:
6. (a) Locate and name the following information on the outline map of Cameroon provided:

**The Equatorial forest zone; river Chari; Cameroon mountain; the Congo basin; the Chad-Cameroon pipeline; one Industrial region**

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the outline map (north at the top). Shade or mark each item in a **different colour or symbol**, **name** it, and give the map a **key**. (1 mark each; the pipeline 2 marks.) The positions are approximate and follow the shape of the outline:

1. **The Equatorial forest zone:** shade the **southern part** of the country, from the southern border northwards to about latitude 5 to 6 degrees North, from the Atlantic coast in the west to the eastern border (the South, Centre, East and Littoral regions and the south of the South-West region).
2. **River Chari:** in the **extreme north** (the tail of the Far North), along the border with Chad, flowing northwards into **Lake Chad** at the tip of the country.
3. **Cameroon mountain (Mount Cameroon):** on the **south-west coast**, close to the Gulf of Guinea, just inland from the coast at the west end of the southern shoreline (the Fako volcano, near Buea).
4. **The Congo basin:** the **south-eastern** corner of Cameroon (the East region, drained by the Sangha river and its tributaries towards the Congo), along the borders with the Central African Republic and the Congo.
5. **The Chad-Cameroon pipeline:** draw a line starting on the **eastern side of the country** (the oil comes from the fields in southern Chad and enters Cameroon in the east), running **west and south-west across the country** through the Adamawa and Centre area to the **Atlantic coast at Kribi** in the south-west, where the oil is loaded onto ships. Mark Kribi as the terminal.
6. **One industrial region:** the **Douala area** on the Atlantic coast (the Littoral region, around the Wouri estuary); the Douala-Edea region is the main industrial area of Cameroon (also accepted: the Yaounde area or Bonaberi).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Describe the climatic characteristics of the equatorial region of Cameroon under **rainfall** and **temperature**.

(3 + 3 = 6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Rainfall (3 marks).**

- The rainfall is **heavy**, often about **1 500 to 2 000 mm or more** a year, and falls in **all months**, because the region is near the equator where hot air rises and brings convectional rain.
- There are **two rainy seasons** (about March to June and September to November) and **two dry seasons** (a short one about July to August and a longer one about December to February), so the dry seasons are short and mild.
- Humidity is high all year, the sky is often cloudy, and thunderstorms are common in the afternoon.

**Temperature (3 marks).**

- The temperatures are **high all year**, with a mean of about **25 degrees C** (the mean monthly temperatures are about 23 to 27 degrees C).
- The **annual range is small** (about 2 to 3 degrees C), because the sun is high in the sky throughout the year and the cloud and humidity reduce the daily and seasonal differences.
- The **daily range is greater** than the annual range, and nights are warm.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Describe **TWO** reasons why livestock rearing is highly carried out in the northern parts of Cameroon.

(4 marks)

(ii) Suggest **TWO** reasons why the Government of Cameroon considers the informal sector important to the economy.

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two reasons for livestock rearing in the north (4 marks).**

1. **Natural environment:** the northern parts have **savanna and Sahel-type grasslands**, with a long dry season, which suit grazing by cattle, sheep and goats; there are fewer **tsetse flies** (which carry sleeping sickness in animals) than in the forest in the south, so the animals stay healthier, and the highlands of the Adamawa plateau have good pasture.
2. **Human and economic factors:** many northern peoples (for example the Fulani/Mbororo) have a **tradition of herding**, there are wide open areas of land, rivers and lakes for water, and there is a **large market** for meat and milk in the towns of the south and in neighbouring countries (Nigeria, Chad), supported by trade routes. Crop farming is less reliable than herding in the dry climate.

**(ii) Two reasons why the informal sector is important (3 marks).**

1. **It creates jobs and incomes:** it employs a very large share of the working population, especially the young and women, and so reduces unemployment and poverty.
2. **It supplies cheap goods and services and adds to the economy:** small traders, craftsmen, hawkers and transporters supply goods and services at low prices to the poor, produce part of the national income and train workers; it does not need much capital and can later be taxed and formalised.
